paragraphs.title: Moses and Aaron Sent Before Pharaoh

easy.question: Who would be Moses’ prophet?
answers: Aaron his brother
Pharaoh
The Israelites
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “Aaron thy brother shall be thy prophet.”

easy.question: What was Moses commanded to say?
answers: Only Pharaoh’s name
Everything the Lord commanded him
The words of the Israelites
easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Moses to speak everything He told him.

easy.question: How old was Moses when he spoke to Pharaoh?
answers: Seventy years old
Eighty-three years old
Eighty years old
easy.explanation: Verse 7 says that Moses was eighty years old.

medium.question: What were Moses and Aaron’s roles before Pharaoh?
answers: Moses received the command, and Aaron spoke to Pharaoh
Aaron received the command, and Moses spoke to Pharaoh
They both spoke without receiving a command
medium.explanation: Moses was to speak the Lord’s words, and Aaron was to deliver them to Pharaoh.

medium.question: In the phrase “I will multiply my signs and my wonders,” what does “wonders” refer to?
answers: Journeys in the wilderness
Miraculous signs and acts
Commands to the king
medium.explanation: The verse refers to signs and wonders that the Lord would perform in Egypt.

medium.question: What would happen after Pharaoh refused to listen to Moses and Aaron?
answers: The Israelites would remain in Egypt unchanged
Moses would become king of Egypt
The Lord would strike Egypt and bring the Israelites out
medium.explanation: The passage says that great judgments would come upon Egypt, followed by Israel’s departure.

challenge.question: What can we understand from Moses being made “a god to Pharaoh” and Aaron being his “prophet”?
answers: Moses represented the Lord’s authority, and Aaron served as his spokesman
Aaron was the true ruler of Egypt
Moses and Aaron did not need to speak to Pharaoh
challenge.explanation: The comparison explains their roles: Moses received the Lord’s message, and Aaron delivered it to Pharaoh.

challenge.question: What numerical detail can be inferred from the ages of Moses and Aaron?
answers: Aaron was three years younger than Moses
Moses was three years younger than Aaron
They were the same age
challenge.explanation: Moses was eighty and Aaron was eighty-three, so Moses was three years younger.

challenge.question: According to the passage, what was one purpose of the signs and wonders in Egypt besides bringing Israel out?
answers: To teach Moses his role
To make Aaron king
To cause the Egyptians to know that the Lord is God
challenge.explanation: Verse 5 says that the Egyptians would know that the Lord is God when He brought Israel out.

questions.question: What can we understand from Moses being made “a god to Pharaoh” and Aaron being his “prophet”?
answers: Moses represented the Lord’s authority, and Aaron served as his spokesman
Aaron was the true ruler of Egypt
Moses and Aaron did not need to speak to Pharaoh
questions.explanation: The comparison explains their roles: Moses received the Lord’s message, and Aaron delivered it to Pharaoh.

questions.question: What numerical detail can be inferred from the ages of Moses and Aaron?
answers: Aaron was three years younger than Moses
Moses was three years younger than Aaron
They were the same age
questions.explanation: Moses was eighty and Aaron was eighty-three, so Moses was three years younger.

questions.question: According to the passage, what was one purpose of the signs and wonders in Egypt besides bringing Israel out?
answers: To teach Moses his role
To make Aaron king
To cause the Egyptians to know that the Lord is God
questions.explanation: Verse 5 says that the Egyptians would know that the Lord is God when He brought Israel out.

easy.question: Who spoke to Moses and Aaron at the beginning of the passage?
answers: The Lord
Pharaoh
The magicians of Egypt
easy.explanation: Verse 8 says that the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron.

easy.question: What did Aaron’s rod become?
answers: Water
A serpent
A tree
easy.explanation: Aaron cast down his rod, and it became a serpent.

easy.question: Who cast down the rod before Pharaoh?
answers: Moses
Pharaoh
Aaron
easy.explanation: The Lord told Moses to have Aaron take his rod and cast it down.

medium.question: What happened after Aaron’s rod became a serpent?
answers: The magicians of Egypt cast down their rods too
Pharaoh immediately listened to Moses
Moses took the rod back
medium.explanation: Pharaoh called the wise men and sorcerers, and they also cast down their rods.

medium.question: What was the result of the magicians’ signs?
answers: Pharaoh released the Israelites
Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he did not listen
Their rods disappeared
medium.explanation: The passage says that Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, so he did not listen to Moses and Aaron.

medium.question: In the verse “Show a miracle for you,” what was Pharaoh asking them to show?
answers: A punishment
A journey
A sign or miracle
medium.explanation: Pharaoh was asking them to demonstrate something extraordinary—a sign or miracle.

challenge.question: What detail shows that Aaron’s sign was greater than the magicians’ signs?
answers: Aaron’s rod swallowed their rods
Aaron cast down the rod before Pharaoh’s servants
Pharaoh called the magicians
challenge.explanation: Although the magicians’ rods became serpents, Aaron’s rod swallowed their rods.

challenge.question: Why was Pharaoh not convinced by the signs, according to the sequence of events?
answers: Moses and Aaron did not speak to him
The magicians performed a similar act, and his heart was hardened
He did not see the rod
challenge.explanation: The magicians performed a similar act, after which Pharaoh’s heart was hardened and he would not listen.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “as the Lord had said” emphasize at the end of the passage?
answers: That the sign happened by accident
That Pharaoh was not present
That the event happened as the Lord had foretold
challenge.explanation: The statement shows that Pharaoh’s hardened heart and refusal to listen occurred as the Lord had said.

questions.question: What detail shows that Aaron’s sign was greater than the magicians’ signs?
answers: Aaron’s rod swallowed their rods
Aaron cast down the rod before Pharaoh’s servants
Pharaoh called the magicians
questions.explanation: Although the magicians’ rods became serpents, Aaron’s rod swallowed their rods.

questions.question: Why was Pharaoh not convinced by the signs, according to the sequence of events?
answers: Moses and Aaron did not speak to him
The magicians performed a similar act, and his heart was hardened
He did not see the rod
questions.explanation: The magicians performed a similar act, after which Pharaoh’s heart was hardened and he would not listen.

questions.question: What does the phrase “as the Lord had said” emphasize at the end of the passage?
answers: That the sign happened by accident
That Pharaoh was not present
That the event happened as the Lord had foretold
questions.explanation: The statement shows that Pharaoh’s hardened heart and refusal to listen occurred as the Lord had said.

paragraphs.title: The Warning of the Plague of Blood

easy.question: Why would Pharaoh not let the people go?
answers: Because his heart was hardened
Because he could not find Moses
Because the people had fled into the wilderness
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Pharaoh’s heart is hardened; he refuseth to let the people go.”

easy.question: Where was Moses to meet Pharaoh in the morning?
answers: In the wilderness
By the river’s bank
At the palace
easy.explanation: Moses was told to stand before Pharaoh by the river’s bank.

easy.question: What would the river’s water become?
answers: Ice
Oil
Blood
easy.explanation: The Lord announced that the water in the river would be turned to blood.

medium.question: Why did the Lord announce the plague upon the river?
answers: Pharaoh had refused to let the people go
Moses had lost his rod
The Egyptians wanted to drink in the wilderness
medium.explanation: Pharaoh had refused to listen, so the Lord would now show His power through the plague upon the river.

medium.question: In the phrase “the Egyptians shall loathe to drink of the water,” what would happen to the Egyptians?
answers: They would rejoice greatly
They would be unable or unwilling to drink
They would pour out the water
medium.explanation: The water would become blood, so the Egyptians would not be able to drink it.

medium.question: Why was Moses told to take the rod in his hand?
answers: To measure the river’s depth
To protect himself from Pharaoh
To strike the river’s water and turn it to blood
medium.explanation: The Lord said that Moses would strike the water with the rod, and it would become blood.

challenge.question: What was the main purpose of the plague according to the words “In this thou shalt know that I am the Lord”?
answers: To show Pharaoh the Lord’s power and identity
To teach the Egyptians to fish
To prepare the people to drink water in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: The plague was meant to make Pharaoh know that the Lord rules over the waters and over creation.

challenge.question: What sequence of results is described after the river’s water becomes blood?
answers: The water is purified, the fish multiply, and the Egyptians drink
The fish die, the river stinks, and the Egyptians cannot drink
Pharaoh releases the people, and the Egyptians leave for the wilderness
challenge.explanation: The passage describes the fish dying, the river becoming foul, and the Egyptians being unable to drink from it.

challenge.question: Why does the passage identify the rod as the rod “which was turned to a serpent”?
answers: To explain that the rod was made of special wood
To say that Moses must turn it into a serpent again
To remind us that it was the same rod previously used as a sign before Pharaoh
challenge.explanation: The description connects the earlier sign before Pharaoh with the rod’s use in the plague.

questions.question: What was the main purpose of the plague according to the words “In this thou shalt know that I am the Lord”?
answers: To show Pharaoh the Lord’s power and identity
To teach the Egyptians to fish
To prepare the people to drink water in the wilderness
questions.explanation: The plague was meant to make Pharaoh know that the Lord rules over the waters and over creation.

questions.question: What sequence of results is described after the river’s water becomes blood?
answers: The water is purified, the fish multiply, and the Egyptians drink
The fish die, the river stinks, and the Egyptians cannot drink
Pharaoh releases the people, and the Egyptians leave for the wilderness
questions.explanation: The passage describes the fish dying, the river becoming foul, and the Egyptians being unable to drink from it.

questions.question: Why does the passage identify the rod as the rod “which was turned to a serpent”?
answers: To explain that the rod was made of special wood
To say that Moses must turn it into a serpent again
To remind us that it was the same rod previously used as a sign before Pharaoh
questions.explanation: The description connects the earlier sign before Pharaoh with the rod’s use in the plague.

paragraphs.title: The Plague of Blood upon Egypt’s Waters

easy.question: Who commanded Moses to tell Aaron what to do?
answers: The Lord
Pharaoh
Pharaoh’s servants
easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Moses to tell Aaron to take his rod and strike the waters.

easy.question: What did the river’s water become?
answers: Dust
Blood
Oil
easy.explanation: The verse says that all the water in the river was turned to blood.

easy.question: Who could not drink water from the river?
answers: The Israelites
Moses and Aaron
The Egyptians
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Egyptians could not drink the river’s water.

medium.question: What did Aaron do to turn the river’s water into blood?
answers: He lifted up the rod and struck the water
He poured blood into the river
He covered the river with stones
medium.explanation: Aaron lifted up the rod and struck the water in the river, and it became blood.

medium.question: In the phrase “the river stank,” what happened to the river?
answers: It dried up
It gave off a foul smell
It became deeper
medium.explanation: The fish died, causing the river to give off a bad smell.

medium.question: What was the correct order of events?
answers: The fish died, then the Lord commanded, and finally Aaron struck the water
The Egyptians drank, then the fish died, and finally the water became blood
The Lord commanded, Moses and Aaron acted, and then the water became blood and the fish died
medium.explanation: First the Lord gave the command; Moses and Aaron obeyed; then the water became blood and the fish died.

challenge.question: What does the list of streams, rivers, ponds, and pools show?
answers: The plague affected many water sources throughout Egypt
The plague occurred only in the river
The plague affected only Pharaoh’s drinking water
challenge.explanation: The list emphasizes that the blood appeared in many water sources throughout Egypt.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “all the waters that were in the river” emphasize?
answers: Only a little water became blood
All the river’s water became blood
Only water outside Egypt became blood
challenge.explanation: The word “all” emphasizes that the plague was complete and widespread, not limited to a small part of the river.

challenge.question: What conclusion follows from the fish dying and the Egyptians being unable to drink?
answers: The plague affected only animals
The Egyptians immediately found another water source
The plague affected both nature and human life
challenge.explanation: The dead fish show harm to the natural world, while the lack of drinking water shows direct harm to people.

questions.question: What does the list of streams, rivers, ponds, and pools show?
answers: The plague affected many water sources throughout Egypt
The plague occurred only in the river
The plague affected only Pharaoh’s drinking water
questions.explanation: The list emphasizes that the blood appeared in many water sources throughout Egypt.

questions.question: What does the phrase “all the waters that were in the river” emphasize?
answers: Only a little water became blood
All the river’s water became blood
Only water outside Egypt became blood
questions.explanation: The word “all” emphasizes that the plague was complete and widespread, not limited to a small part of the river.

questions.question: What conclusion follows from the fish dying and the Egyptians being unable to drink?
answers: The plague affected only animals
The Egyptians immediately found another water source
The plague affected both nature and human life
questions.explanation: The dead fish show harm to the natural world, while the lack of drinking water shows direct harm to people.

paragraphs.title: Pharaoh Ignores the Plague and the Egyptians Search for Water

easy.question: Who also performed the same act with their enchantments?
answers: The magicians of Egypt
The Israelites
The people of the wilderness
easy.explanation: The verse says that the magicians of Egypt did the same with their enchantments.

easy.question: What did Pharaoh do after seeing what happened?
answers: He went to the river
He returned to his house
He called the people
easy.explanation: The passage says that Pharaoh turned and went into his house.

easy.question: How many days passed after the river was struck?
answers: Three days
Ten days
Seven days
easy.explanation: The passage says, “And seven days were fulfilled.”

medium.question: Why did the Egyptians dig around the river?
answers: To find gold
To obtain drinking water
To escape from Egypt
medium.explanation: They could not drink the river’s water, so they dug to find water elsewhere.

medium.question: In the phrase “the magicians of Egypt did so with their enchantments,” what did they use?
answers: Secret arts or magic
A loud voice
Great speed
medium.explanation: The phrase indicates that the magicians tried to imitate the act through their magical arts.

medium.question: What was the result of Pharaoh’s hardened heart?
answers: He released the Israelites
He asked the Egyptians for water
He did not listen or pay attention to this either
medium.explanation: The passage connects Pharaoh’s hardened heart with his refusal to listen and his failure to take notice of the situation.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the Egyptians dug around the river?
answers: The river’s water was not fit to drink
The river disappeared completely
Egypt had no wells at all
challenge.explanation: They could not drink from the river, so they had to search for water another way.

challenge.question: What sequence of events is described in the passage?
answers: The Egyptians dug, then the magicians acted, and finally Pharaoh returned home
The magicians acted, Pharaoh returned home, and the Egyptians dug for water
Pharaoh returned home, the river filled with water, and then the magicians acted
challenge.explanation: First the magicians acted, then Pharaoh went home, and afterward the Egyptians dug around the river.

challenge.question: What does Pharaoh’s response reveal about his attitude toward what was happening?
answers: He immediately understood the seriousness of the situation
He ignored the situation and did not change his mind
He was afraid and left Egypt
challenge.explanation: Pharaoh paid no attention even after the Egyptians had to dig for water, showing his stubbornness and disregard.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the Egyptians dug around the river?
answers: The river’s water was not fit to drink
The river disappeared completely
Egypt had no wells at all
questions.explanation: They could not drink from the river, so they had to search for water another way.

questions.question: What sequence of events is described in the passage?
answers: The Egyptians dug, then the magicians acted, and finally Pharaoh returned home
The magicians acted, Pharaoh returned home, and the Egyptians dug for water
Pharaoh returned home, the river filled with water, and then the magicians acted
questions.explanation: First the magicians acted, then Pharaoh went home, and afterward the Egyptians dug around the river.

questions.question: What does Pharaoh’s response reveal about his attitude toward what was happening?
answers: He immediately understood the seriousness of the situation
He ignored the situation and did not change his mind
He was afraid and left Egypt
questions.explanation: Pharaoh paid no attention even after the Egyptians had to dig for water, showing his stubbornness and disregard.

paragraphs.title: The Warning of the Plague of Frogs

easy.question: Whom did the Lord tell Moses to go to?
answers: Pharaoh
Aaron
The Israelites
easy.explanation: The Lord told Moses, “Go unto Pharaoh.”

easy.question: What was Pharaoh required to do?
answers: Build furnaces
Let the people of Israel go
Gather frogs
easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Pharaoh to let His people go so that they could serve Him.

easy.question: Which plague is described in these verses?
answers: Locusts
Blood
Frogs
easy.explanation: The verses describe frogs coming up from the river and spreading throughout the land.

medium.question: What would happen if Pharaoh refused to let the people go?
answers: Frogs would cover all his land
The river would dry up
Moses would return to Midian
medium.explanation: The Lord warned that frogs would cover all of Pharaoh’s land if he refused.

medium.question: In the phrase “if thou refuse to let them go,” what would Pharaoh be doing?
answers: Hurrying
Refusing
Rejoicing
medium.explanation: The phrase describes Pharaoh’s refusal to release the people.

medium.question: What can we understand from the mention of Pharaoh’s houses, bedrooms, servants’ houses, and ovens?
answers: The frogs would remain only in the river
The frogs would appear only where Moses was
The plague would spread widely and reach everyone
medium.explanation: The list shows that the frogs would enter homes and private places rather than remain only in the river.

challenge.question: What order of spread is described in the passage?
answers: From the river to the houses and various places
From the houses to the river only
From the wilderness into Egypt
challenge.explanation: First the river would swarm with frogs, and then they would come up and enter many homes and places.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “if thou refuse to let them go” show about the relationship between Pharaoh’s action and the plague?
answers: The plague had already ended
The plague was presented as a possible result of Pharaoh’s refusal
Pharaoh had asked for the plague
challenge.explanation: The word “if” presents a condition: if Pharaoh refused, the plague of frogs would come.

challenge.question: Which detail in the list of places especially emphasizes the frogs’ intrusion into daily life?
answers: The river
The border of the land
The ovens and kneading troughs
challenge.explanation: Mentioning the ovens and kneading troughs shows that the frogs would reach even places where food was prepared and stored.

questions.question: What order of spread is described in the passage?
answers: From the river to the houses and various places
From the houses to the river only
From the wilderness into Egypt
questions.explanation: First the river would swarm with frogs, and then they would come up and enter many homes and places.

questions.question: What does the phrase “if thou refuse to let them go” show about the relationship between Pharaoh’s action and the plague?
answers: The plague had already ended
The plague was presented as a possible result of Pharaoh’s refusal
Pharaoh had asked for the plague
questions.explanation: The word “if” presents a condition: if Pharaoh refused, the plague of frogs would come.

questions.question: Which detail in the list of places especially emphasizes the frogs’ intrusion into daily life?
answers: The river
The border of the land
The ovens and kneading troughs
questions.explanation: Mentioning the ovens and kneading troughs shows that the frogs would reach even places where food was prepared and stored.
